routes.label: Count observer-angle intervals from the six side normals

changes.rationale: The apothem is h=sqrt(3). A side with outward normal phi is fully visible exactly when r*cos(theta-phi)>h, except zero-measure tangent boundaries. Write cos(beta)=h/r. For beta in (60, 90) degrees, three consecutive normals are visible on six disjoint intervals of width 2beta-120 degrees, and four normals cannot fit inside width 2beta<180. Thus the probability is 6beta/180-2, equal to 1/2 at beta=75 degrees. This gives r=sqrt(3)/cos75=3sqrt(2)+sqrt(6), D. Reuse the final separated-D uniform arc-probability mapping with its explicit opaque-convex-polygon visibility model; no new inverse-trig node is inferred from the angle notation.

answerCheck.reason: The hexagon apothem is sqrt(3). A side with outward normal phi is entirely visible iff r*cos(theta-phi)>sqrt(3). Let cos(beta)=sqrt(3)/r. For beta in (pi/3,pi/2), exactly-three visibility consists of six disjoint intervals of width 2beta-2pi/3; four normals cannot fit into width 2beta<pi. Thus probability is 6beta/pi-2. Setting it to 1/2 gives beta=75 degrees and r=sqrt(3)/cos75=3sqrt(2)+sqrt(6). Cases beta<=pi/3 give zero three-side probability.
